hook.text: Halloween comes from Samhain—the Celtic new year. On October 31, the veil between living and dead thinned.

buildup.text: Celts lit bonfires and wore costumes to confuse wandering spirits. Disguise was protection, not play.

discovery.text: Jack-o'-lanterns come from an Irish tale of a man too clever for hell. He wanders forever with a turnip light.

twist.text: Christianity absorbed Samhain. All Saints' Day on November 1 honored the holy dead. Hallow's Eve remained.

climax.text: Modern Halloween disguises its origin. A candy holiday was once the year's most spiritually dangerous night.

punchline.text: The costume started as a shield.
